precepts.text: The slayer that kills his neighbour ignorantly, as when the axe head slips from the helve, flees to the city of refuge and lives, for he was not worthy of death.
precepts.point: But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile, thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die. Men would run and grab the horns of the altar, but wilful murder found no refuge there.

note.label: Exodus 21: The Judgments Set Before Israel

precepts.why:
“And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.” Deuteronomy gives the case: “And this is the case of the slayer, which shall flee thither, that he may live: Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past; As when a man goeth into the wood with his neighbour to hew wood, and his hand fetcheth a stroke with the axe to cut down the tree, and the head slippeth from the helve, and lighteth upon his neighbour, that he die; he shall flee unto one of those cities, and live”.

Why he must flee: “Lest the avenger of the blood pursue the slayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and slay him; whereas he was not worthy of death, inasmuch as he hated him not in time past.” The man who killed his neighbour ignorantly, with no hatred in time past, was not worthy of death, so a place was appointed where he could live.

But the man who came presumptuously upon his neighbour to slay him with guile had no such place. Men would run and grab the horns of the altar, but wilful murder found no refuge there: “thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.”

precepts.text: The avenger pursues the slayer while his heart is hot; without refuge he would overtake and slay a man who was not worthy of death.
precepts.point: The city of refuge keeps the manslayer alive until he stands before the congregation in judgment, so the trial can discern between murder and manslaughter before the avenger reaches him.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The cities of refuge were for “the slayer” “which killeth any person at unawares”: he did not mean to do it; it was an accident that resulted in a death, and accidental deaths are of the Lord, beyond our control. Refuge means a condition of being safe or sheltered from pursuit, danger or trouble, and the manslayer is being pursued, for someone has the right to avenge the death of the one who was killed.

“Lest the avenger of the blood pursue the slayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and slay him; whereas he was not worthy of death, inasmuch as he hated him not in time past.”

The avenger pursues while his heart is hot. Without a city of refuge close enough, he would overtake and slay a man who was not worthy of death, one who hated him not in time past. The city of refuge keeps the manslayer alive “until he stand before the congregation in judgment”, so the trial can discern between murder and manslaughter before the avenger reaches him.

precepts.text: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin; at the mouth of two or three witnesses is the matter established.
precepts.point: The rule stood first for sins worthy of death and then had to become the principle for every matter: two or three witnesses establish any accusation of iniquity or sin.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The rule of witnesses stood first for sins worthy of death, and then it had to become the principle for every matter. “One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity, or for any sin, in any sin that he sinneth: at the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.”

Not only murder: any iniquity, any sin, in any sin that he sinneth. Two or three witnesses establish any accusation, so that no man is condemned on the word of one who might be lying.

precepts.text: Ye have heard that it hath been said, an eye for an eye; but Christ says resist not evil, meaning do not seek revenge, not that you allow yourself to be beaten down.
precepts.point: Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

precepts.why:
In this time under Moses it was “life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.” If a man knocked out your tooth, the recompense was exact, and it went through the judges one way or another; thus saith the law.

Christ spoke on this saying: “Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also.” He spoke on it because exact retaliation between men creates a never-ending cycle of vengeance and hatred.

Resist not evil means do not seek revenge. Turning the other cheek does not mean letting somebody beat you down into the dirt; it means when somebody does something to you, do not come back later seeking revenge.

precepts.text: Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord: do not avenge yourself, for revenge only brings judgment on you.
precepts.point: Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head; the wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.” This is why Christ said resist not evil where the law said eye for eye and tooth for tooth.

Seeking revenge only brings more judgment on your own head. The wise course is to let it go and let the Most High repay, for vengeance belongs to him: give place unto wrath, and he will repay.

precepts.text: Moses gave the instruction to separate cities of refuge in the midst of the land; in Joshua 20 Joshua is applying the law.
precepts.point: Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
Now that every tribe had its inheritance, the cities of refuge had to be instituted, “whereof I spake unto you by the hand of Moses”. Here is where Moses spoke it: “When the Lord thy God hath cut off the nations, whose land the Lord thy God giveth thee, and thou succeedest them, and dwellest in their cities, and in their houses; Thou shalt separate three cities for thee in the midst of thy land”. The coasts of the land were to be divided into three parts, “that every slayer may flee thither.”

Moses gave the instruction; in Joshua 20 Joshua is applying the law, now that the nations are cut off and Israel dwells in their cities.

precepts.text: The case of the slayer: two neighbours go into the wood to hew wood, the axe head slips from the helve and lights upon his neighbour that he die; he hated him not in time past, so he was not worthy of death.
precepts.point: Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“That the slayer that killeth any person unawares and unwittingly may flee thither”. Unwittingly means unknowingly; remember the word wittingly in Genesis 48, where Israel guided his hands knowing what he was doing. This is accidental death, not intentional murder. “And this is the case of the slayer, which shall flee thither, that he may live: Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past”. Two neighbours go into the wood to hew wood, “and the head slippeth from the helve, and lighteth upon his neighbour, that he die; he shall flee unto one of those cities, and live”. It is like leaving a co-worker shut in the freezer by mistake because you were focused on going home.

Notice the scripture says slayer, not murderer: a slayer may be innocent, it may have been a mistake or self-defense, so there are stipulations and laws for his case. He “was not worthy of death, inasmuch as he hated him not in time past.”

“Lest the avenger of the blood pursue the slayer, while his heart is hot, and overtake him, because the way is long, and slay him”. The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.

precepts.text: But if any man hate his neighbour and lie in wait and smite him mortally, the elders of his city shall fetch him from the refuge and deliver him to the avenger of blood; thine eye shall not pity him.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The murderer cannot run to a city of refuge to lay low; those cities were not established for him. “But if any man hate his neighbour, and lie in wait for him, and rise up against him, and smite him mortally that he die, and fleeth into one of these cities: Then the elders of his city shall send and fetch him thence, and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die. Thine eye shall not pity him”.

Even today a killer can cross the border into another jurisdiction and go free, and that is evil; but when Israel controlled the land you could not cross a border to get away with murder, for the elders would deliver you right back to the city you came from. Your sin will find you out. That is how “thou shalt put away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, that it may go well with thee.”

precepts.text: Life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth: that was the judgment instituted in that time; today we are under different laws of the land, and you forgive your brother seventy times seven.
precepts.point: The avenger of blood is a family member of the one killed, and while his heart is hot he is not thinking logically; he is guided by his emotions, and that is how you end up rendering evil for evil. Heart is hot is the same way we talk today, I was hot, I am heated: our forefathers and foremothers spoke the same way.

note.label: Joshua 20: The Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
“And thine eye shall not pity; but life shall go for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.” That was the judgment instituted in that time: the murderer delivered to the avenger of blood, life for life, without pity.

Today we are under different laws of the land, and you forgive your brother seventy times seven. But the cities of refuge in Joshua were built under that judgment, which is why the murderer had no refuge in them and the slayer who killed unawares did.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not remove thy neighbor's landmark which they of old time have set in thine inheritance.
precepts.point: They drive away the ass of the fatherless and take the widow's ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way, and the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job says, “Some remove the landmarks; they violently take away flocks, and feed thereof.” The law forbids it: “Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour’s landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance, which thou shalt inherit in the land that the Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it.”

The landmark was set of old time in the inheritance the Lord gave. Removing it is the wicked moving into your land and naming it after themselves. That is the crime of the oppressor Job is describing, and times are not hidden from the Almighty.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour's landmark; this is why each tribe's inheritance is marked off by a border.
precepts.point: From the north end the tribes are named, and the first portion by its border is for Dan; each tribe receives a bordered portion of land.

note.label: Ezekiel 48: The Land Divided and the Gates of the Tribes

precepts.why:
From the north end the tribes are named by their borders, “From the north end to the coast of the way of Hethlon, as one goeth to Hamath, Hazar–enan, the border of Damascus northward, to the coast of Hamath”, and the first portion is for Dan. Each tribe receives a bordered portion of land.

That is why the borders matter. “Thou shalt not remove thy neighbour’s landmark, which they of old time have set in thine inheritance, which thou shalt inherit in the land that the Lord thy God giveth thee to possess it.” Each tribe's inheritance is marked off by a border, a landmark set in the inheritance, and it is not to be moved.

The key is that you hated him not in time past: it was not premeditated. You got into a fight, you got jumped, you were defending yourself, and a life was lost that you never intended to take. Righteous judgment under God's law says the judgment for that should not be stiff; your life should not be taken away, because your intent was not to kill.

points: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or for any sin. At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established.

You understand what a witness is. There must be a witness; don't just take a man's word for it. Oh, I know he's your friend; don't just take his word for it. Our people lie, and always add to what happened to make themselves feel better. As a judge, you cannot be like that. Two or three witnesses: let the matter be established.

If a false witness rises up, the judges make diligent inquisition. Whatever he thought to do to his brother shall be done to him, and so evil is put away from Israel.

points: When the Most High cut off the nations of the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, the Jebusites, the Perizzites, and the Girgashites, and Israel succeeded them and dwelt in their cities and houses, Israel was to separate three cities in the midst of the land and prepare the way to them.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: This law goes into accidental death, what the Bible sometimes calls manslaughter. An Israelite who accidentally killed another could flee to one of these three cities of refuge, where the avenger of blood could not seek him out and kill him there to revenge the blood of his nearest of kin.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: Whoso killeth his neighbour ignorantly, whom he hated not in time past, means he did not mean to do it; it was an accident. The example given is two men hewing wood, and the axe head slips from the helve and strikes the neighbour that he die: he shall flee to one of those cities and live.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: The avenger of blood is the nearest of kin, and while his heart is hot he may pursue and overtake the slayer because the way is long. But the slayer was not worthy of death, because he hated him not in time past; there was no premeditation, no intention to kill.
Accidents happen, and the Most High put laws in place for when these things happened. If it was for sure an accident, the man is not worthy of death, as the scripture says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: If the Lord enlarge thy coast as he sware unto the fathers, then three more cities were to be added. As Israel grew and possessed more of the land of Canaan, more cities of refuge were established where a slayer could flee from the avenger of blood.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: The purpose is stated plainly: that innocent blood be not shed in the land which the Lord giveth thee for an inheritance, and so blood be upon thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: This gives the distinction between an accident and intentional killing; this is describing murder. He hated his neighbour and lay in wait for him: he devised a scheme, waited for the right opportunity and the right time, rose up against him, and smote him mortally that he died.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: The murderer cannot then run to a city of refuge to lay low. Those cities were not established for him; they were established so retaliation did not come on those who accidentally brought harm to somebody. The elders of his own city shall fetch him from there and deliver him into the hand of the avenger of blood, that he may die.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: Thine eye shall not pity him: putting away the guilt of innocent blood from Israel is what makes it go well with the nation.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: What is a landmark? It pays to use tools outside the scriptures, because what good is reading the Bible without understanding of the words written in it. The Zondervan Bible Dictionary defines a landmark as an object, stone, or post used to mark the boundary of a field, and notes that removal of landmarks was prohibited by the Mosaic law.

The landmark establishes the boundaries of a man's property, where it begins and where it ends. A man who keeps nudging his neighbour's landmark over little by little until he has taken an acre is stealing land; the dictionary notes it was considered equal to theft.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: One witness shall not rise up against a man for any iniquity or any sin. One man alone saying he saw a theft is not proof; anybody can come and lie and get people put to death, imprisoned, or beaten.

At the mouth of two witnesses, or at the mouth of three witnesses, shall the matter be established. It has to be clear-cut; two or three solid witnesses, not one solid witness and a shaky witness. We deal with facts.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: When a false witness rises up, both men in the controversy stand before the Lord, before the priests and the judges of those days. False accusation is real: people will lie on a man to cover themselves, and false witnesses arise among your own people as well, which is part of why the nation fell into captivity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: The judges shall make diligent inquisition: they get to the bottom of the matter and find out exactly who is telling the truth, who is lying, and what the facts are. A judge cannot judge a matter off what one person says; each side tells the story in his own favour, so you must examine the whole matter, question both sides against each other, and decipher the truth. Diligent inquisition is what separates a good judge from a bad judge; a lazy or partial judge makes false judgment.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: If the witness is found false, then shall ye do unto him as he had thought to have done unto his brother. Accuse a man falsely of stealing, and the judgment for stealing comes on you; accuse him falsely of adultery or another sin punishable by death, and you are put to death, because that is what you intended for your neighbour. So is evil put away from Israel.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses

points: The judgment is public and it teaches: those which remain shall hear and fear, and shall henceforth commit no more any such evil among you.

note.label: Deuteronomy 19: Cities of Refuge and True Witnesses
